Age
āj
n. (the length of life; the season of maturity; rendering Hebrew yom, seybah, Greek hēlikia)
From Latin aetas, through French âge. In the Authorized Version age is nearly always a man's span of years, not an epoch of history.

Biblical Definition

In the Authorized Version age is chiefly personal: the measure of a man's life, and a thing God gives. The LORD promises Abram, “thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age” (Gen 15:15), and of David it is written that “he died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour” (1Ch 29:28). A good old age is not a biological accident in Scripture; it is a covenant blessing, one of the things promised to those who honour father and mother. Age also marks the point at which a man answers for himself — the parents of the healed blind man push the questioning back onto their son, “he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself” (Joh 9:21) — and it marks the point past which nature can no longer help: Sarah “received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised” (Heb 11:11). That last is the doctrine in a sentence. Age is the boundary of what flesh can do, and therefore the place where faith in a promising God does its clearest work.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines age as the whole duration of a being, the latter part of life, a mature or advanced period, and a generation or century of men.

expand to see more

AGE, n. The whole duration of a being, whether animal, vegetable or other kind.

2. That part of the duration of a being, which is between its beginning and any given time.

3. The latter part of life, or long continued duration; oldness.

4. A certain period of human life, marked by a difference of state; as the age of infancy, of youth, of manhood.

5. The period when a person is enabled by law to do certain acts for himself; as, to come of age.

Key Scripture

Gen 15:15 — "And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age."

1Ch 29:28 — "And he died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour: and Solomon his son reigned in his stead."

Joh 9:21 — "But by what means he now seeth, we know not; or who hath opened his eyes, we know not: he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself."

Heb 11:11 — "Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised."

Modern Corruption

Old age has been reclassified from a crown to a problem — a decline to be delayed, disguised, or shortened — and the honour Scripture commands toward the aged has gone with it.

expand to see more

Scripture calls the hoary head a crown of glory when it is found in the way of righteousness, and commands a man to rise up before the hoary head. A culture that prices usefulness and appearance above all can only read age as loss, and so treats the aged as a cost. From that follows the warehousing of the old, the abandonment of the fifth commandment's duties toward parents, and finally the argument that a life which has stopped producing may be ended early for mercy's sake. Each step is a further denial that the days of a man belong to God and not to his usefulness.

The opposite error is a sentimental cult of youth in the church itself, where the counsel of grey-headed members is quietly set aside for the sake of energy and style. Titus 2 assumes the reverse traffic: aged men sober and sound in faith, aged women teaching the young women. Recover the biblical estimate and both errors fall. A good old age is a blessing to be sought, an honour to be given, and a resource the congregation cannot do without.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew seybah (H7872), grey hair, old age; Greek hēlikia (G2244), stature or age — the measure of a life, and the boundary where faith takes over from nature.

expand to see more

Hebrew seybah (H7872) — hoary head, grey-headedness, old age; “a good old age” (Gen 15:15) and the crown of glory of Pro 16:31.

Hebrew yom (H3117) — day; in the plural, a man's days, hence his age — “full of days” (1Ch 29:28).

Greek hēlikia (G2244) — age, stature, maturity; “he is of age” (Joh 9:21) and Sarah “past age” (Heb 11:11).

Usage

"“Thou shalt be buried in a good old age” — length of days named as covenant blessing."

"“He is of age; ask him” — the point at which a man answers for himself."

"“When she was past age, because she judged him faithful” — where nature ends, faith begins."
